detections.evidence_quote: When you're in these types of delusion, every billboard, every Bible verse, license plate, song, everything can become a personal message for you

detections.evidence_quote: I want to give you a very practical framework for how to differentiate an intrusive thought from psychosis
detections.summary: Host frames an episode on delusion and psychosis tied to the Lindsay Clancy trial and promises a framework distinguishing intrusive thoughts from psychosis.

detections.evidence_quote: Held with a level of conviction that is resistant to contradictory evidence and is disconnected from consensual reality
detections.summary: Host contrasts everyday inaccurate beliefs with delusion and defines delusion as conviction resistant to contradictory evidence and disconnected from consensual reality.

detections.evidence_quote: I want to be clear: these things are not interchangeable
detections.summary: Host corrects the interchangeability of intrusive thoughts, delusion, and psychosis.

detections.evidence_quote: This is the first misconception: people believe things every single day that are inaccurate

detections.evidence_quote: some of the reality testing questions being labeled as narcissistic and gaslighting
detections.summary: Host corrects the social-media tendency to label reality-testing questions as narcissistic and gaslighting.

verification_candidates.claim_text: In these types of delusion, everything—billboards, Bible verses, license plates, songs—can become a personal message.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: every billboard, every Bible verse, license plate, song, everything can become a personal message for you
verification_candidates.rationale: Describes a symptom of delusion that could be assessed against clinical descriptions.

verification_candidates.claim_text: In delusion, every contradiction also confirms the belief.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: even worse, now every contradiction also confirms the belief
verification_candidates.rationale: A specific claim about how delusions treat contradictory evidence; relevant to understanding psychosis.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Spiritual and religious frameworks can sometimes become wrapped into psychosis.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: why spiritual and religious frameworks can sometimes become wrapped into the psychosis
verification_candidates.rationale: Claims a relationship between religious/spiritual content and psychosis that could be examined clinically.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Repeated, sustained misinterpretation is not necessarily psychosis but could eventually lead to psychosis.

verification_candidates.rationale: Claims sustained misinterpretation can progress to psychosis; clinically checkable and consequential.

verification_candidates.claim_text: A delusion is a belief held with conviction, resistant to contradictory evidence, and disconnected from consensual reality.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Held with a level of conviction that is resistant to contradictory evidence and is disconnected from consensual reality
verification_candidates.rationale: Offers a definition of delusion that can be checked against diagnostic criteria.
